findings.description: The function returns options.get(key) or default, which substitutes default when the stored value is falsy (e.g., 0, False, '', None). According to the contract, default should only be used when the key is absent.
findings.evidence: candidate.setting({'x': 0}, 'x', 9) incorrectly returns 9 instead of 0; candidate.setting({'x': ''}, 'x', 9) incorrectly returns 9 instead of ''.

review.summary: The implementation incorrectly uses truthiness to determine if a key exists, causing falsy values to be ignored and default used.
